title: npm run doctor diagnoses no checkout-level blocker: not a shallow clone, not missing deps
body:
Found by the 2026-09-02 repository audit, from this session's own start-up experience in a
fresh remote checkout. Third item in the same family as bug_0594 and audit item
`shallow-clone-disables-triage-staleness-aging`.

## The gap

`npm run doctor` is the environment doctor — the thing an agent or operator runs to learn
why this checkout cannot do something. It reports three sections: which dev agents are on
PATH, which playtest providers can launch here, and the state of the corpus/queue/bucket.

It checks NOTHING about the two conditions that actually stop a fresh checkout from
working, both of which this session hit before doing any work:

1. **Truncated git history.** A shallow clone (Claude Code on the web clones this way,
   and so does any `git clone --depth 1`) makes `npm run health` fail at step 2 with 771
   TRACE_REFERENCE_MISSING findings. bug_0594 fixed the misdiagnosis inside that gate, so
   the message now names the remedy — but only once you have already run the bar and
   watched it fail. Doctor is where that should have been visible first, and
   `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` is a one-line probe. The same truncation
   silently disables triage's STALE_AFTER_BUILDS aging (filed separately).

2. **Dependencies not installed.** AGENTS.md is explicit that `npm run health` needs UI
   deps too ("Install UI deps with `npm --prefix ui install` (required for
   `npm run health`)"), so a checkout with root deps but no `ui/node_modules` fails the
   bar at the ui:typecheck step, well after the cheap checks pass. With no root
   node_modules at all, `.mcp.json`'s server command (`npm --silent run mcp`) cannot
   start, and a client discovers only a connection failure — the exact symptom this
   session saw. Neither is reported anywhere.

Doctor already has the right instincts everywhere else: it prints the honest middle state
per provider and names the module doing the trusting. It just never looks at the checkout
itself.

## Suggested checks

A short "Checkout" section, before "Dev loop":

- `git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository` → if true: history is truncated; `npm run health`
  and `npm run qa:triage` are both degraded; run `git fetch --unshallow`.
- `node_modules` present at the repo root → if absent: `npm install`; the MCP server
  declared in .mcp.json cannot start without it.
- `ui/node_modules` present → if absent: `npm --prefix ui install`, required for
  `npm run health`'s ui:typecheck step.
- optionally the Node major version against the documented 22+ floor.

## Testability

Unlike bin/triage.ts, bin/doctor.ts guards its `main()` behind the argv check, so it is
importable and its helpers are already unit-tested directly (see the comment above that
guard, and tests covering `onPath`). A checkout-facts helper taking the root as an
argument can be tested against fixture directories without a clone, the same way
bug_0594's `shallowHistory` option is driven.

Worth doing together with the triage item, since both want the same shallow probe and a
shared, testable git-history helper under src/ would serve
scripts/verify-bug-traces.ts, bin/triage.ts and bin/doctor.ts at once — that shared module
is the reason both were filed rather than patched in place.
